w10_T4_002923: At the start of the day a bike shop had 108 helmets on its racks. During the morning a delivery brought 44 helmets, and before lunch a returned order added 75 more. In the afternoon a cycling club bought 213 helmets for its members. Later that afternoon a second delivery brought 55 helmets, and a customer returned 12. In the evening a supplier dropped off another 43. How many helmets does the shop have?
w10_T4_002924: Ivan had 40 fence posts in his yard, and his neighbour Petra gave him 9 more, far fewer than he already had. A farm sale added another 44 posts to the same pile. Ivan then used 25 posts on the paddock gate. Every post still in the pile needs 4 nails to fix it in place. How many nails does Ivan need?
w10_T4_002926: A gym had 93 lockers in its old changing room and added 7 more. A second changing room was then built with exactly the same number of lockers, so the gym now has 2 identical rooms. Each locker holds 7 towels. The gym has 3 swimming lanes in the pool. A cupboard by the door holds another 59 towels, and the gym counts its linen in single towels rather than in bundles. How many towels can the gym hold in total?
w10_T4_002928: On Monday morning a bakery baked 51 loaves in each of its 7 ovens. Before lunch 275 loaves were sold at the counter, and a hotel collected 61 more. The bakery weighs its dough in grams rather than in kilograms, and half of the staff start work at dawn. In the afternoon every loaf still in the shop was cut into 7 thick slices. In the evening each of those slices was cut into 4 fingers for the tasting table. How many fingers of bread did the bakery have?
w10_T4_002938: Selim had 92 flowerpots in his yard. He sold 57 pots at the market, and his sister Dila took 26 for her balcony, fewer than he had sold. Each pot he has left holds 8 bulbs. A tray on the bench holds 36 more bulbs, a sack in the shed holds 64, and a friend brought over 46 in a box. The nursery counts its stock in single bulbs rather than in trays. How many bulbs does Selim have?
w10_T4_002941: A stadium had 130 flags in store, and the club bought 64 more. Every flag is fastened with 4 clips. A box on the shelf holds 9 spare clips of the same type. Each clip costs 7 pence to replace. The main stand seats 12000 people. What is the total cost, in pence, of replacing all of the stadium's clips?
w10_T4_002943: A brickworks fired 170 bricks in each of its 5 kilns. Of those bricks, 153 cracked in the cooling and were discarded. A neighbouring yard sent 63 bricks to make up the shortfall. Every brick weighs 5 pounds. The yard's chimney is 30 metres tall, and half of the kilns are over a century old. A lorry then took away 612 pounds of those bricks. How many pounds of brick are left?
w10_T4_002945: A school chess club had 13 boards at the start of term and bought 54 more. It lent 51 boards to a tournament that never sent them back. A sponsor then doubled the number of boards the club still had. The club sent 28 boards to the summer camp, and 1 more was broken in the minibus. The club meets in room 7 every Thursday. How many boards does the club have?
w10_T4_002956: A wholesaler had 235 boxes of matches and sold 59 of those boxes. Each box holds 3 packets, and each packet holds 3 bundles. Every bundle contains 6 booklets, and each booklet holds 8 matches. The warehouse has 14 shelves along its back wall. Half of the stock is kept at the far end. How many matches does the wholesaler have?
w10_T4_002962: A youth theatre had 27 costumes on its rail, and 2 of them were beyond repair. A donation added 52 costumes to the same rail. The wardrobe manager then set up a second rail holding exactly the same number, so 2 identical rails now stand backstage. A hire company delivered 71 more costumes. The theatre has 4 dressing rooms. A touring show then took 37 costumes away. How many costumes are backstage?
w10_T4_002965: A council had 169 street lamps on the high street and removed 125 old ones. It installed 48 new lamps and put 22 more along the alley. Each lamp holds 4 bulbs. Every bulb uses 9 watts, and the council reports its use in watts rather than in kilowatts. The high street is 700 metres long. How many watts do the lamps use?
w10_T4_002966: Nour picked 77 lemons, and her cousin Sami picked exactly as many, doubling the pile they had between them, so neither of them had more than the other. They sold 147 lemons at the roadside stall, which prices its fruit in cents rather than in dollars. They then threw away 5 bruised lemons. A neighbour gave them 65 lemons from her own tree. How many lemons do they have?
w10_T4_002967: A print room produced 133 pamphlets on each of its 9 machines. Every one of those pamphlets was then copied 5 times for the mailing. A drawer held 46 spare copies, and another office sent over 53 more. Each copy is 4 pages long. The building has 3 lifts. How many pages are there in all of those copies?
w10_T4_002971: A camp store took in 61 crates of food, and a second delivery doubled the number of crates it held. The crates were then split equally between the 2 camps in the valley. The north camp later received 79 more crates of its own. Every crate holds 4 boxes, and each box holds 4 tins. How many tins does the north camp have?
w10_T4_002974: Rosa knitted 39 hats for the winter fair, and her friend Jonah knitted 44, so Jonah made more hats than Rosa did. They bought 9 beads to decorate every hat. A box was dropped on the stairs and 130 of the beads were lost. A craft shop donated 44 beads, and a school sent another 42. The village hall costs 15 pounds an hour to hire. How many beads do they have now?
w10_T4_002975: A school ordered 5 boxes of exercise books with 61 books in each box. It sent 75 of the books over to the annexe. The stationery cupboard gave up 52 more books, a parent donated 35, and a bookshop added 18. The school has 9 classrooms. How many exercise books does the school have?
w10_T4_002976: Omar had 51 seed trays and gave 39 of them to his neighbour Rina, who ended up with far more trays than he kept. Each tray Omar kept holds 6 seedlings. Slugs then destroyed 64 of his seedlings. Rina tripled the number of seedlings Omar had left by giving him some of her own. Omar planted out 21 seedlings in the garden, and half of the bed is still bare. A friend gave him 6 more seedlings. How many seedlings does Omar have?
w10_T4_002979: A dairy fills 131 bottles on each of its 6 filling lines. The night shift added another 44 bottles to the same batch. Every bottle pours 4 cups, and each cup holds 5 ounces, since the dairy measures its milk in ounces rather than in pints. A dozen inspectors visited the plant that week. How many ounces of milk are in the batch?
w10_T4_002982: A courier drove 80 kilometres on each of the 7 days of her round. Of that distance, 196 kilometres were on private roads and cannot be claimed. The firm pays 5 pence for every kilometre claimed, and expenses are always paid in pence rather than in pounds. Her van is 3 years old. A toll charge of 127 pence was then deducted from her claim. How many pence does the courier receive?
w10_T4_002983: On Monday morning a workshop had 147 reels of thread, and a delivery added 26 more. In the afternoon the staff measured them and found that every reel holds 8 metres of thread. Half of all that thread was sent to the sister workshop, and the rest stayed on the bench. A tangle then wasted 29 metres of the thread that had stayed. In the evening a supplier sent over 39 metres more. How many metres of thread are on the bench?
w10_T4_002989: A stationery plant puts 18 pencils into every pack, and each box holds 7 packs. A carton holds 5 of those boxes, and a pallet holds 8 cartons. One shipping container was loaded with 8 pallets, counted in single pencils rather than in boxes. All of those pencils were then shared equally among the 6 shops in the chain. How many pencils did one shop receive?
w10_T4_002992: Hana had 13 concert tickets, and her cousin Milo handed her 66 more, far more than she had started with. She sold 77 of the tickets at the stall and lost 1 on the bus home. The printer then delivered 33 replacement tickets. She divided all her tickets into 2 equal piles, one for each door of the hall, and kept the pile for the side door. Ushers collected 13 tickets at that door during the show. How many tickets from her pile were left?
w10_T4_002996: A quarry cut 172 slabs on each of 3 days. Every slab was then split into 2 equal pieces. A builder bought 334 of those pieces and drove them away. Each piece still at the quarry was cut into 3 tiles. Every tile weighs 3 kilograms, and the quarry gives its weights in kilograms rather than in tonnes. What is the total weight, in kilograms, of the tiles at the quarry?
w10_T4_003011: On Monday morning a nursery sowed 121 seeds in each of its 5 trays. By the end of the week 546 of those seeds had failed to come up. In the afternoon the gardener counted 7 stems on every plant that had grown. Each stem carries 6 flowers, and half of the greenhouse is shaded at midday. In the evening she worked out that every one of those flowers will set 7 new seeds. How many new seeds will the plants set?
w10_T4_003013: A youth club shared 117 tins of paint equally among its 3 halls. The main hall found that 10 of its tins had dried out and threw them away. A donation then brought 75 more tins to the main hall. Each tin covers 5 square metres, and the club measures its walls in square metres rather than in square feet. Half of the hall has already been painted once. How many square metres can the main hall's paint cover?
